## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 25-juan late-Míng / early-Qīng revision of the *Wǔdēng huìyuán* 五燈會元 ([KR6q0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0012)), updated and re-organised under a strict Línjì-orthodoxy programme. Compiled by [通容](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E5%AE%B9) Fèiyǐn Tōngróng, abbot of Tiāntóngshān 天童山 (where his teacher [密雲圓悟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%86%E9%9B%B2%E5%9C%93%E6%82%9F) Mìyún Yuánwù had also been abbot) and one of the most polemically active Línjì masters of the late Míng. The work generated immediate and lasting controversy with the Cáodòng line, who saw it as a tendentious re-routing of their own lineage history.

**Abstract**

Tōngróng updated the *Wǔdēng huìyuán* template with two innovations: first, he extended the genealogy through the Yuán and Míng down to his own generation; second, and more aggressively, he re-attributed several Sòng-era Cáodòng masters whose lineage placement had previously been settled, arguing that they actually descended from Línjì-line teachers. The Cáodòng response — *Wǔdēng yántǒng jiěhuò biān* 五燈嚴統解惑編 ([KR6q0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0020)), Tōngróng's own self-defence pamphlet, plus several anti-pamphlets from the Cáodòng side — turned the *Yántǒng* into the centerpiece of a major mid-seventeenth-century inter-lineage textual dispute. The case is treated at length in modern Chán historiography as a paradigmatic example of late-imperial Chán lineage politics.

The work was printed in the Jiāxīng 嘉興 canon and entered the Xuzangjing through that channel.
